title: Analysts See Jio Listing Pop of Up to Twenty Percent After Record IPO
excerpt: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion offer, priced at 1,065-1,119 rupees a share for a $108.3 billion valuation, opens October 21 with analysts expecting 15% to 20% listing gains.
body:
• Analysts say Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion IPO is fairly valued at about $108.3 billion, leaving room for listing gains of 15% to 20%.
  • The sale opens October 21 at 1,065 to 1,119 rupees a share, with trading expected to start October 28 — it would be India's biggest IPO.
  • A strong debut would make Jio India's fourth-largest listed company, behind Reliance Industries, Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank.
  • Longer-term returns hinge on converting a huge telecom base into higher-margin digital, cloud and AI revenue, analysts say.

Jio Platforms, the digital and telecom arm of Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries, is priced to leave something on the table for new investors, analysts said ahead of what will be India's largest initial public offering. The company is seeking a valuation of about $108.3 billion from a $3.2 billion share sale, and market indicators point to potential listing gains of 15% to 20%, according to Reuters.

That expected debut would outpace the first-day performance of other recent large listings, including the National Stock Exchange of India, Hyundai Motor India and Tata Capital. The offer opens on October 21 and the shares are expected to begin trading on October 28.

Pricing and the Offer

Jio set a price band of 1,065 rupees to 1,119 rupees per share — $11.19 to $11.76 — in a company filing on Wednesday, Reuters reported. At the top of that band the company targets a valuation of 10.3 trillion rupees, about $108.25 billion. Parent Reliance Industries rose 2.8% on Thursday after the band was set, while shares of rival Bharti Airtel were also trading 3.3% higher, a sign investors are repricing the whole sector ahead of the listing.

"We expect demand to be resilient across investor categories."

— Aishvarya Dadheech, Founder and Chief Investment Officer, Fident Asset Management

Why Analysts See Room to Rise

The argument for a listing pop rests on relative value. Jio is India's largest telecom operator by subscribers and is backed by Meta and Google, with businesses spanning mobile, broadband, enterprise services, cloud, digital apps and data centres. Its main listed rival, Bharti Airtel, is valued at about $118 billion, reflecting its operations in Africa and its network infrastructure holdings. Against that benchmark, analysts say Jio's asking price does not fully charge for its scale.

The Reliance name itself is part of the demand case. Dadheech told Reuters the group's weight in the market should support demand across retail, institutional and other investor categories, even at a record issue size for India.

The Question After Listing Day

Analysts were clear that a first-day gain is the easier part. Sustained returns, they said, will depend on whether Jio converts its enormous subscriber base and data leadership into higher-quality, higher-margin revenue — paid digital services, enterprise contracts, cloud and AI offerings rather than low-priced connectivity alone.

"The market will want to see how Jio translates its enormous subscriber base, data leadership and digital ambitions into sustained earnings growth."

— Arun Kejriwal, Founder, Kejriwal Research and Investment Services

Dharmesh Kant, head of equity research at Cholamandalam Securities, pointed to data centres and low-earth-orbit satellite communications as earnings contributors over time, while noting both remain longer-term opportunities. Nomura, which rates Bharti as its top sector pick, has argued that with the era of easy subscriber gains ending for Indian telecom companies, tariff increases will become the primary driver of earnings growth across the industry — a dynamic that would shape Jio's numbers as a listed company in its own right.

What Happens Next

The immediate sequence is fixed: subscriptions open October 21, and trading is expected to begin October 28. A debut at the top of the indicated range would place Jio immediately among India's most valuable listed companies and set a new benchmark for large Indian offerings, surpassing Hyundai Motor India's 2024 listing as the country's biggest to date.
